instructions:
1. Sit on the floor and extend your legs straight, raised just off the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell with both hands close to your chest and lean back slightly with a straight back.
3. Rotate your torso to the right and move the dumbbell toward the floor beside your right hip.
4. Rotate back through the center, then rotate to the left and move the dumbbell beside your left hip.
5. Return to the center. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Lead the rotation with your obliques, not your arms.
2. Keep your legs raised and together for stability.
3. Exhale as you twist, inhale as you return to center.
4. Do not round your lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
2. Keep your shoulders level and your posture upright.
3. Walk forward in a straight line, keeping the dumbbell close to your body.
4. Keep a neutral spine and resist leaning toward the loaded side.
5. After the set distance or time, switch the dumbbell to the other hand. Repeat.
tips:
1. Resist sideways bend; brace your core against the load.
2. Keep your shoulders level and do not let the loaded shoulder shrug.
3. Take even, controlled strides.
4. Use a weight that challenges your grip without breaking posture.

instructions:
1. Stand between two benches with a wide stance and toes pointed slightly outward.
2. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, letting it hang between your legs.
3. Lower into a wide squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
4. Drive through your heels to stand back up and squeeze your glutes at the top.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking over your toes; do not let them collapse inward.
2. Keep your chest up and back straight.
3. Use the extra depth off the benches to load the inner thighs.
4. Drive through your heels, not your toes.

instructions:
1. Stand on a sissy squat platform with feet shoulder-width apart and lower legs secured by the pads.
2. Hold a dumbbell close to your chest with both hands.
3. Lower your body by bending at the knees and leaning back, keeping hips and torso in a straight line.
4. Lower until your thighs are almost parallel to the floor.
5. Drive through your knees to return to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips straight to load the rectus femoris in the stretch.
2. Move slowly and with control on the way down.
3. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
4. Brace your core to keep your torso and hips aligned.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest.
2. Press your palms firmly into the dumbbell to engage your chest.
3. Extend your arms straight out in front at shoulder height, keeping the dumbbell squeezed between your palms.
4. Pull the dumbbell back to your chest under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep constant inward pressure on the dumbbell to load the chest.
2. Press forward in a smooth, controlled line.
3. Keep your torso tall and core braced.
4. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
